step1_figure.circuit_type: Synchronous Buck Converter (DC-DC Converter) with Non-Overlapping Gate Driver and Bootstrapped High-Side Driver
step1_figure.description: The netlist implements a step-down synchronous DC-DC buck converter. Subcircuit SUB_1 generates non-overlapping gate drive signals ('Up' and 'Down') via NAND-inverter logic and incorporates the bootstrapped driver from Fig. 18.39 to provide boosted gate drive to the NMOS high-side switch (xmu), feeding an LC filter (L1=100uH, C1=7.5nF) and resistive load (Rload=40Ω).

output_voltage.description: DC steady-state output voltage of the buck converter

source.reference: DC-DC Buck Converter Ideal Transfer Characteristics

equation.explanation: In continuous conduction mode (CCM), the average output voltage is proportional to the duty cycle D multiplied by the supply input voltage Vs.
equation.assumptions: CCM operation, ideal switching, D = 0.5, Vs = 1.8V

sky130_expected.calculation: Vs = 1.8 V, with nominal 50% duty cycle (D = 0.5): Vout = 0.5 * 1.8 V = 0.90 V. Accounting for switch conduction drops across xmu and xmd (Ron ~ 0.5-1.5 Ω with W/L = 200u/0.15u), Vout drops slightly by ~10-30 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A 50% duty cycle at 1.8V nominally yields 0.9V minus small switch and parasitic IR drops.

output_voltage_ripple.description: Peak-to-peak voltage ripple at the output node Vout

equation.formula: Delta_Vout = Delta_IL / (8 * C1 * fs) = (Vs - Vout) * D / (8 * L1 * C1 * fs^2)
equation.explanation: Peak-to-peak output ripple voltage governed by the inductor current ripple integrated across the output capacitor C1.
equation.assumptions: Ideal capacitor ESR, switching frequency fs = 10 MHz, L1 = 100 uH, C1 = 7.5 nF, D = 0.5

sky130_expected.reasoning: Large inductance (100 uH) relative to switching frequency results in very low inductor ripple and sub-5mV ripple.

inductor_ripple_current.description: Peak-to-peak ripple current flowing through inductor L1

equation.explanation: Change in inductor current during switch on-time ton = D / fs.
equation.assumptions: fs = 10 MHz, L1 = 100 uH, D = 0.5, Vs = 1.8V, Vout = 0.9V

sky130_expected.reasoning: Inductor current ripple is tightly bounded by high switching frequency and 100 uH inductance.

power_efficiency.description: Power conversion efficiency of the buck converter

equation.explanation: Ratio of average load power delivered to total average power drawn from the input source Vs.
equation.assumptions: Steady-state operation evaluated over integral switching periods

sky130_expected.calculation: Pout = (0.88 V)^2 / 40 Ω = 19.36 mW. Conduction losses P_cond = Iload^2 * Ron = (22 mA)^2 * 1 Ω ~ 0.5 mW. Switching and driver dynamic losses ~ 1.5 mW. Total Pin ~ 21.5 mW -> Efficiency ~ 19.36 / 21.5 * 100% ≈ 90%.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Synchronous rectification avoids diode forward voltage drops, giving high efficiency (85-92%) at tens of mA load.

output_power.description: Average power delivered to the resistive load

equation.explanation: Power dissipated in the 40-ohm load resistor at steady-state output voltage.

filter_corner_frequency.description: Resonant frequency of the output LC low-pass filter

source.reference: Q of an LC circuit, Index p. 1171

equation.explanation: Natural undamped resonance of the second-order low-pass filter formed by L1 and C1.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined purely by passive components L1 and C1.

step3_testbench.description: Complete ngspice transient testbench for the synchronous buck converter, measuring output voltage, ripple, load current, power efficiency, and output power over a steady-state window.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Synchronous Buck Converter Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameter definitions for transistors
.param W_xmu=200u L_xmu=0.15u
.param W_xmd=200u L_xmd=0.15u
.param W_xm1=10u L_xm1=0.15u
.param W_xm2=10u L_xm2=0.15u
.param W_xm3=10u L_xm3=0.15u
.param W_xm4=10u L_xm4=0.15u
.param W_xm1i=3u L_xm1i=0.15u
.param W_xm2i=6u L_xm2i=0.15u
.param W_xm1a=3u L_xm1a=0.15u
.param W_xm2a=6u L_xm2a=0.15u
.param W_xm8=6u L_xm8=0.15u
.param W_xm11=3u L_xm11=0.15u
.param W_xm12=3u L_xm12=0.15u

* Power Supplies
VDD VDD 0 DC 1.8
Vs Vs 0 DC 1.8

* PWM Input Clock (10 MHz, 50% duty cycle)
Vin Vin 0 PULSE(0 1.8 0 1n 1n 49n 100n)

* DUT Power Stage and Output Filter
xmu Vs N001 N002 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xmu} l={L_xmu}
xmd N002 N003 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xmd} l={L_xmd}
C1 Vout 0 7.5e-09
X_X1 Vin Vs N001 N003 SUB_1
L1 N002 Vout 0.0001
Rload Vout 0 40.0

* Subcircuits from design
.subckt SUB_1 In Vs Up Down
  X_X1 N004 Up Vs Fig18_39
  X_X2 N005 Down Vs INV_240_80
  X_X3 N001 N004 Vs INV_240_80
  X_X4 N003 N001 Vs INV_30_10
  X_X5 N007 N005 Vs INV_30_10
  X_X6 N006 N007 Vs INV_30_10
  X_X7 N002 N003 Vs INV_30_10
  X_X8 In N008 Vs INV_30_10
  X_X9 In N005 N002 Vs NAND_2
  X_X10 N001 N008 N006 Vs NAND_2
.ends SUB_1

.subckt Fig18_39 In Out VDD
  xm1i N001 In 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1i} l={L_xm1i}
  xm2i N001 In VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2i} l={L_xm2i}
  C2 N002 B 5p
  xm1a N002 N001 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1a} l={L_xm1a}
  xm2a N002 N001 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2a} l={L_xm2a}
  xm3 Out N001 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
  xm4 Out N001 B B sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm4} l={L_xm4}
  C1 N001 A 1p
  xm2 B A VDD 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
  xm1 A B VDD 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
.ends Fig18_39

.subckt INV_240_80 In Out VDD
  xm1 Out In 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
  xm2 Out In VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
.ends INV_240_80

.subckt INV_30_10 In Out VDD
  xm1 Out In 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm1} l={L_xm1}
  xm2 Out In VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm2} l={L_xm2}
.ends INV_30_10

.subckt NAND_2 A B Out VDD
  xm3 out B VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm3} l={L_xm3}
  xm8 out A VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 w={W_xm8} l={L_xm8}
  xm11 N001 B 0 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm11} l={L_xm11}
  xm12 out A N001 0 sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 w={W_xm12} l={L_xm12}
.ends NAND_2

* Control Block for Execution and Automated Measurement
.control
  set wr_singlescale
  * Run transient analysis matching Baker's LTspice timing (up to 20 us)
  tran 50p 20u 19.7u

  * Steady-state output voltage measurements
  meas tran vout_avg avg v(vout) from=19.7u to=20.0u
  meas tran vout_max max v(vout) from=19.7u to=20.0u
  meas tran vout_min min v(vout) from=19.7u to=20.0u
  let vout_ripple = vout_max - vout_min
  print vout_avg vout_ripple

  * Inductor current ripple
  meas tran il_avg avg i(L1) from=19.7u to=20.0u
  meas tran il_max max i(L1) from=19.7u to=20.0u
  meas tran il_min min i(L1) from=19.7u to=20.0u
  let il_ripple = il_max - il_min
  print il_avg il_ripple

  * Power and Efficiency calculations
  meas tran pin_avg avg @Vs[i] from=19.7u to=20.0u
  let p_in = -pin_avg * 1.8
  let p_out = (vout_avg * vout_avg) / 40.0
  let efficiency = (p_out / p_in) * 100
  print p_out p_in efficiency

  quit
.endc
.end
